hero.title: DeFi from first principles: build the pieces, understand the risks
hero.subtitle: Calculate swaps by hand, read an automated market maker line by line, put numbers on impermanent loss and liquidation, test a yield claim and learn the patterns that keep repeating in exploits. Every task is checked and explained.
hero.outcomeLine: After this course you can explain, calculate and critically review core DeFi mechanisms. It does not give financial advice.

faq.q: Is this financial or investment advice?
faq.a: No. It is education. It does not recommend any product, and DeFi can lose all your money. Never use money you cannot afford to lose.
Only on a test network, for learning. They are not audited and omit protections that real protocols need.
You should be comfortable with basic Solidity and tokens, for example from the earlier courses in this series.

activities.title: Read a stablecoin reserve statement
activities.objective: Calculate whether a stablecoin is fully backed and how good its reserves are. (Educational: not an assessment of any real coin.)
activities.scenario: An issuer reports its reserves and the number of tokens in circulation. Work out the backing ratio and the quality of the reserves.
steps: In B7 add up the reserves.
In B8 work out the backing ratio: reserves divided by tokens in circulation, as a percentage.
In B9 work out the percentage of reserves held in cash and treasury bills.
In B10 show Fully backed if the ratio is at least 100, otherwise Under-backed.
In B11 work out the surplus or shortfall.

activities.title: Work out a swap and its price impact
activities.objective: Use the constant-product formula to find the output of a swap and how much worse than the quoted price it was.
activities.scenario: A pool holds 1,000 A and 2,000,000 B. A trader sells 20,000 B for A. The fee is 0.3%, so 99.7% of the input counts. (Teaching figures.)
steps: In B7 work out the input after the fee: input times 997 over 1,000.
In B8 work out the output of A: reserve A times B7, divided by (reserve B plus B7).
In B9 work out the average price paid: input divided by output.
In B10 work out the price before the trade: reserve B over reserve A.
In B11 work out the slippage as a percentage: (B9 over B10 minus 1) times 100.

checks.label: B7 is the input after fee
B8 is the A received
checks.explain: Reserve A times input over (reserve B plus input).

checks.label: B9 is the average price
B10 is the price before
B11 is the slippage
checks.explain: How much worse than the starting price.

activities.title: Calculate impermanent loss
activities.objective: Use the standard formula to compare a pool position with holding, and see how much fee income would offset the gap.
activities.scenario: A provider deposits 10,000 rupees worth of two tokens, half in each. The price of one token doubles relative to the other. (Teaching figures; real pools differ.)
steps: In B7 work out the impermanent loss as a fraction: 2 times the square root of the ratio, divided by (1 plus the ratio), minus 1.
In B8 show it as a percentage.
In B9 work out the value if the tokens had simply been held: half the deposit times (1 plus the ratio).
In B10 work out the value of the pool position: B9 times (1 plus B7).
In B11 work out the gap, which is the fee income needed to break even against holding.

checks.label: B7 is the loss fraction
B8 is the loss in percent
B9 is the value if held
checks.explain: Half the deposit times one plus the ratio.

checks.label: B10 is the pool value
checks.explain: Held value times one plus the loss.

checks.label: B11 is the gap

cells.A11: Gap to make up with fees (rupees)

activities.title: How safe is this loan?
activities.objective: Calculate borrowing capacity, health factor and the price fall that would trigger liquidation. (Education only.)
activities.scenario: A user deposits collateral worth 100,000 rupees. The market allows borrowing up to 75% of its value and liquidates at 80%. They have borrowed 60,000 rupees.
steps: In B7 work out the maximum borrowing allowed.
In B8 work out the health factor: collateral times liquidation threshold over 100, divided by the debt.
In B9 work out the percentage fall in the collateral's value that would trigger liquidation.
In B10 work out how much more could still be borrowed.
In B11 show Liquidatable below 1, Risky below 1.5, otherwise Comfortable.

checks.label: B7 is the maximum borrowing
B8 is the health factor
B9 is the price fall
checks.explain: How far collateral can fall before the threshold is reached.

checks.label: B10 is the headroom
B11 is the status
checks.hint: =IF(B8<1,"Liquidatable",IF(B8<1.5,"Risky","Comfortable"))

Mention smart contract risk and the possibility of losing the deposit.
State that this is education and not financial advice.

activities.title: Final project: write a DeFi protocol design and risk review
activities.objective: Produce a professional design and risk review of a simple DeFi component, with numbers, safeguards and honest limits.
activities.scenario: Choose a simple component such as a swap pool, a lending market or a vault, and write the design and risk review you would give a team before they build it on a test network.
steps: Add a Heading 1 with the component's name and 'design and risk review'.
Add Heading 2 sections: Purpose, How it works, Key numbers, Safeguards, Threats and failure cases, What is out of scope, Limits of this review.
Under Key numbers include at least three figures such as fees, ratios or limits.
Under Safeguards list at least four in bullets.
Under Threats and failure cases mention an oracle or price risk, a liquidity risk and a smart contract risk.
State that it is for a test network, not audited and not financial advice.
Keep it between 350 and 700 words.
